text:
Diego: heads up — we got a sharp spike in Xid79 and Xid48 on apne1 a10 racks starting ~02:15 UTC, looks concentrated to rack apne1-a10-07, ~6 cards reporting. https://mon.redwood/alerts/3529
monitoring-bot: ALERT fired: nv_xid_errors_total{region=\"apne1\", rack=\"apne1-a10-07\"} increased by 420 in 10m (severity: high)
Lee: ugh. any batch job or new rollout around that time?
Diego: no deployments. small tenant traffic spike only. I pulled recent jobs, nothing heavy.
Maria: can you paste the query you used? want to cross-check with telemetry backend.
Diego: PromQL I ran:
```
sum by (gpu_id, xid_code) (increase(nv_xid_errors_total{region=\"apne1\"}[1h]))
```
Diego: and a quick BigQuery grab for last 2h:
```sql
SELECT gpu_host, xid_code, COUNT(*) AS cnt
FROM `infra.gpu_events`
WHERE region = 'apne1' AND event_ts BETWEEN TIMESTAMP_SUB(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 2 HOUR) AND CURRENT_TIMESTAMP()
GROUP BY gpu_host, xid_code
ORDER BY cnt DESC
```
Sophie: can we check ECC counters too? Xid79 sometimes aligns with ECC flips but also with PCIe/IOS issues. run `nvidia-smi -q -d ECC` on the hosts?
Aj: +1. Also check kernel oops and pcie reset logs: `dmesg | grep -E 'PCIe|AER|Xid'` and `/var/log/kern.log` around 02:10-02:20.
Lee: I see pattern: the top 3 GPUs have both Xid79 and Xid48 concurrently. hints at a shared subsystem — maybe PCIe switch or upstream root port.
Maria: rack-level NICs had a driver update last week (nv-mlx4 hotfix). could be related. any NIC errors?
Diego: I pulled NIC counters, small rx align errors on toplevel switch for that rack at 02:14.
Sophie: timeline aligns. Hypothesis: a transient PCIe reset (or PLX switch) causing decode errors (Xid48) and subsequent ECC recoveries (Xid79). we should repro with stress tests and capture hw counters.
Aj: vendor note: if multiple card slots show simultaneous Xid codes, suspect upstream peer (switch/PCIe root). we should avoid replacing cards blindly.
Diego: propose plan: 1) soft-drain rack during low traffic window (2h), 2) run targeted stress + collect `nvidia-smi -q`, `pcie_aer` and kernel traces, 3) swap PCIe riser on a single host as experiment, 4) open case with NVIDIA + switch vendor.
Lee: fine, when's low traffic window for APAC? 05:00-07:00 UTC looks quiet.
Maria: +1 for 05:30 UTC maintenance window. ops-bot can schedule soft drain?
ops-bot: Scheduling soft drain for apne1-a10-07 at 05:30 UTC for 120 minutes. Command queued: `/infra drain rack apne1-a10-07 --mode=soft --duration=120m`
Diego: I'll prepare collection scripts. snippet to run after drain:
```bash
for h in $(cat hosts.txt); do ssh $h "sudo dmesg -T | tail -n 200 > /tmp/dmesg.post; sudo nvidia-smi -q -d ECC > /tmp/nv_ecc; sudo journalctl -k --since \"-30m\" > /tmp/kern30m"; scp $h:/tmp/* ./collected/$h/; done
```
Sophie: also capture `lspci -vvv` and `sudo ethtool -S <nic>` on the toplevel host. and set `nv_peer_mem` debug logs if available.
Aj: I'll assemble a small CANARY job to run during the drain that reproduces long sequences of small batches (more likely to trigger decode path).
Maria: I'll open the vendor ticket after we collect traces; attaching runbook and initial cluster diag. include these aggregated counts and the PromQL result.
Diego: quick summary actions: [1] ops-bot schedule drain 05:30 UTC (done), [2] Sophie/Diego collect hw + kernel logs during drain, [3] Aj run canary workload and stress PCIe path, [4] Maria open vendor ticket with logs + counters, [5] avoid immediate GPU replacements until vendor input.
Lee: thanks. keep this thread updated with initial collection results and vendor case id. :thumbsup:
Maria: will update ticket id here once created.
monitoring-bot: Note: increased alert sensitivity for apne1 has been temporarily suppressed during maintenance window (05:25-07:45 UTC) to avoid noisy repeats.
Diego: OK will post first collection dump here after 05:40 UTC.
Sophie: one more note — if vendor recommends board-level swap, plan for single-host outage and test before broad action.
Aj: logging that we should also look at historical coincidence map: correlation between Xid spikes and recent NIC driver rollouts in apne1 (last 30 days). I'll run the query and post results.
Diego: thanks team — will follow up with artifacts.
